idiom_name: pact-jvm consumer DSL driven from ScalaTest suites
implementation_notes: Scala has no Pact client of its own, so the JVM libraries fill both roles: the realization is pact-jvm's consumer DSL (ConsumerPactBuilder with PactDslJsonBody matchers, or the JUnit 5 extension) hosted in ScalaTest suites, with the mock server URL injected into the client under test, and pact-jvm's provider side replaying the contracts against the running service. There is no Scala-specific DSL to lean on - the API is Java-shaped - so keep one interaction builder per provider and let ScalaTest's matchers assert on the client's parsed result.
pitfalls: Java functional-interface plumbing leaks into Scala: runConsumerTest takes a PactTestRun SAM, so the client call must return Unit and assertions must be ScalaTest matchers rather than JUnit assertions.
pact.rootDir is a JVM system property read by the forked test JVM (sbt: javaOptions in Test), so contract publishing silently finds nothing when it is set in the wrong scope.

A Scala client built on a type-level stack (case classes plus http4s/circe or sttp) still has to accept the mock URL through configuration; a hard-coded base URL makes the client untestable against the contract.
